settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: FileUtils.checkReadAllowed is invoked before parsing and blocks local file usage when file access is unset, but it does not affect HTTP URLs nor external-entity resolution.
config.getOrDefault("failOnError", true) only controls exception handling (Xml.java lines 62, 92-103); it does not restrict parsing behavior.
No repository code explicitly enables DTD or external entity resolution, which is neutral evidence but confirms no explicit hardening either.
candidates.description: In src/main/java/apoc/load/Xml.java, xmlXpathToMapResult() creates a DocumentBuilderFactory (line 65) and only sets setNamespaceAware(true) and setIgnoringElementContentWhitespace(true) (lines 66-67), then builds a DocumentBuilder (line 68) and parses content fetched from a caller-supplied URL via Util.openInputStream (line 74). No hardening features (FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, 'http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl', XMLConstants.ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/SCHEMA, setExpandEntityReferences(false)) are set. A crafted document containing a DOCTYPE with external/internal entities could therefore cause external resource resolution and/or entity expansion during parse(). Root cause: parser hardening is absent. Impact direction is information disclosure (local/remote file read via entity) and SSRF via entity resolution. This is reported as a candidate, not confirmed exploitation.
missing_evidence: No runtime test found that parses an XML document with a DOCTYPE/external entity through this procedure to demonstrate resolution.
JDK/parser version and default entity-resolution behavior at deployment are not verifiable from source alone.
Whether the procedure is exposed to an untrusted role (procedure security allow-list / dbms.security settings) is configured outside this repository.
preconditions: Caller can invoke the XML-loading procedure with an arbitrary url (e.g. a hostile HTTP endpoint, or a file:// path when file access is enabled).
The XML parser in the deployed JDK expands/resolves DTD external or parameter entities by default.
candidates.title: apoc.load.xml DocumentBuilderFactory parses caller-supplied XML URL without disabling DTD/external entities (candidate XXE/SSRF)

counter_evidence: FileUtils.checkReadAllowed(url) restricts only local file access and does not prevent HTTP fetching nor entity resolution.
The xmlSimple procedure is deprecated (deprecatedBy = "apoc.load.xml") but still exposed (Xml.java lines 53-58).
candidates.description: In src/main/java/apoc/load/Xml.java, a static shared XMLInputFactory FACTORY is created at line 39. getXMLStreamReaderFromUrl(String url) checks FileUtils.checkReadAllowed(url) and then opens a connection to the URL, setting only FACTORY.setProperty(XMLInputFactory.IS_COALESCING, true) before createXMLStreamReader(urlConnection.getInputStream()) (lines 121-126). It never sets XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false or IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false. This reader is used by procedures that consume the caller-supplied url (e.g. the deprecated apoc.load.xmlSimple at lines 53-58, which calls xmlToMapResult). Because the factory is static and shared, any per-call unsafe configuration also persists across calls. A hostile XML stream fetched from the supplied URL could therefore trigger DTD processing / external entity resolution (XXE/SSRF) during event reading. Root cause: missing parser hardening plus reuse of a globally configured factory.
missing_evidence: No test in src/test/java/apoc/load demonstrates external-entity resolution through these procedures.
StAX parser implementation/version and its default entity behavior are not determinable from the source.
Whether the shared static factory is ever reconfigured elsewhere at runtime was not exhaustively traced.
preconditions: Caller can invoke a procedure that reads XML from an attacker-controlled url.
The StAX implementation honors DTD/external entities by default (no SUPPORT_DTD=false configured).
candidates.title: Shared static XMLInputFactory parses caller-supplied URL stream with DTD/external-entity support not disabled (candidate XXE/SSRF)
